transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Nearly eight months since the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran, NPR has learned both
countries are preparing plans for another possible attack on the Islamic Republic after
the midterms.
NPR's Hadil Al-Shalchi reports Iran says it is ready.
Foreign Foreign Minister Abbas Arakchi told Iranian state media that just as his country
is prepared for diplomacy, it's prepared for war.
Arakchi said that "any scenario is conceivable, including the possibility of an attack by
the U.S. and Israel."
The U.S. and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran in early November,
according to a person briefed on the matter speaking to NPR in the condition of anonymity.
Iranian state media also quoted a security source saying that if Iranian officials or
civilian infrastructure were attacked, Iran would retaliate by targeting U.S. interests
in the region, as well as the infrastructure and assets of countries participating in the
war.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
President Trump heads to Iowa today to continue campaigning for Republican candidates ahead
of the November midterm elections.
Last night, the president was in South Carolina for a rally for Republican Senator Darlene
Graham.
Here's NPR's Frank Ordonez.
President Trump urged the very enthusiastic crowd at Clemson University to show up at
the polls to help elect Darlene Graham and other Republicans.
Trump spoke of Graham carrying on the legacy of her brother, who was a close ally to the
president.
I asked Darlene to run.
And after a little thought, because it's a very big decision, it really is, it's a big
decision because I love it.
She said yes, and I was very happy about it.
Graham is in a surprisingly tight race for such a red state running against Democrat
Annie Andrews, but Trump has struggled politically as the war in Iran has dragged on, and gas
prices have surged.
Frank O. Ordonez, NPR News.
In a regulatory filing today, the medical lab operator Quest Diagnostics reveals its
systems were the target of a cyberattack.
Found out about it this week, Quest Diagnostics says some of its patients' records were likely
compromised.
Shares and electric vehicle maker Tesla are down after the company reported flat revenue
for the third quarter compared with the same quarter last year, here's NPR's Willow Rubin.
Most of Tesla's money comes from selling cars, especially the Model 3 and the Model Y. And
those sales dropped during the quarter, compared with the same period last year.
In a call with analysts, CEO Elon Musk didn't talk much about cars, though.
Instead, he focused on the kinds of technologies Tesla is investing a ton in, like robotaxes
and building humanoid robots.
Musk was also asked about his announcement on Tuesday's SpaceX earnings call that the
two companies had launched special committees to explore the possibility of merging.
But he said they weren't going to take more questions about it.
And he said talking about it was like "tap dancing through a minefield."
Willow Rubin, NPR News.
This is NPR.
A federal judge is ordering President Trump to sit for a deposition in his $10 billion
defamation lawsuit against the BBC and must do so by December 11th.
The president accuses the publicly funded British broadcaster of editing a speech he
delivered to supporters ahead of the insurrection on January 6, 2021, to make it seem as if
he was directly calling for violence.
The BBC apologized for the edits and top executives resigned, however, the BBC denies that it
defamed President Trump.
New research offers some evidence that psychedelics may fight inflammation in people with diseases
such as Parkinson's.
NPR's Will Stone reports on the findings published in the medical journal JAMA Psychiatry.
It's an area of psychedelic research that hasn't received as much attention, but experiments
in animals consistently show some psychedelics have powerful anti-inflammatory effects.
Now, a team at UCSF has published data from a small study of people with Parkinson's.
They saw markers of inflammation in the blood declined after they took psilocybin, and that
persisted 30 days after.
Dr. Ellen Bradley at UCSF says the findings need to be confirmed in larger trials.
This gives us this initial biological signal to investigate.
People with neurodegenerative conditions are typically excluded from studies on psychedelics,
but Bradley says they're finding these substances may actually help symptoms.
Will Stone, NPR News.
US stocks trading lower, the NASDAQ is down 547 points, more than 2%.
This is NPR.

topics.text: U.S. and Israel reportedly planning possible new attack on Iran in early November
Iran's foreign minister says the country is prepared for war as well as diplomacy
President Trump campaigns in South Carolina for Senator Darlene Graham amid tight race
Quest Diagnostics discloses cyberattack that likely compromised some patient records
Tesla shares fall after flat third-quarter revenue; Musk discusses robotaxis and humanoid robots
Federal judge orders President Trump to sit for deposition in $10 billion BBC lawsuit by December 11
Study suggests psilocybin reduces blood inflammation markers in people with Parkinson's
U.S. stocks slide, with the NASDAQ falling more than 2% in afternoon trading
